# Step AE: each script's own key, not its file name

Lead (2026-11-19, Orbit TOOLS-361, follow-up to TOOLS-358): key the safety-net copies, the B-roll links and lists and the "Check" flags by each script's own identity instead of its file name, with old name-keyed data still readable. Then background scripts may keep copies again, so marks and asks survive a reload. Behind the scenes: no prototype; nothing new to see.

## What it does

- **A key per script** (`public/script-keys.js`, new, no DOM). A file on the computer gets an id of its own the first time it opens here, kept with its handle in IndexedDB (`fileIds`: `[{ handle, id }]`, the file opened here most recently first, at most 200, so a full list lets go of the files not opened for longest, and never of a file a tab has in use); its key is `file:<id>`. The same file opened again (the switcher hands over a fresh handle) is found with `isSameEntry` and keeps its key; another file of the same name gets another. A script in the browser goes by its name (names there are unique, and a rename moves its keys, as before); a script without a file (the demo, a file opened where files can't be saved) goes by its name too. Ids are given under a Web Lock (`script-editor:file-ids`), so two tabs never give one file two ids. Where storage refuses, or the list can't be read, a file goes by its name, as before, and the list is not written (review round 1).
- **What goes by the key** (`app.js`): the draft (`script-editor:draft:<key>`, with its open asks, marked changes and `broll` "Check" flags), the B-roll link (`broll:<key>`) and a B-roll list kept in the browser (`brollList:<key>`). `saving.js` takes `keys: { of(handle, name), adopt(handle) }`: a left script's failed save keeps its draft under its own key, and Save as moves the script's keys to the picked file's own key (`adopt`): a new file gets a new key, also when it has the same name in another folder; a file that has a key keeps it.
- **Background scripts keep their draft again** (`persistKept`): a script kept aside writes its draft under its own key as it leaves, before and after each write of an answer. After a reload, opening it brings back the agent's marked change with Undo on the agent's tag, its open asks and its "Check" flags; words that could not be written come back as "Unsaved changes". The dot itself does not come back (the scripts kept aside live in the tab's memory). `keptWords`, `on.keepsWords` and `noDraft` (TOOLS-358's choice B) are removed.
- **Old data stays readable.** Once per browser profile, before any file opens (`migrate`), the files on the recent list get ids and take what was kept under their name (`legacyPlan`): each gets a copy of the B-roll link and list, the newest of that name takes the draft, and the name lets go of them. A file seen for the first time later takes what is still under its name. A name that a script in the browser has stays with that script: at the move the files on the list get a copy of its B-roll link and list only, and later a new file of that name takes nothing (review round 1). Deleting a browser script drops its keys unless another script that goes by that name is known; files on the computer no longer count (`nameShared`). The demo keeps its own.
- **A full storage loses nothing** (second look, gpt-6.1-sol): a draft moves to a new key only once it is written there (`drafts.move` gives false and keeps it), the move fills only places never written (the list before its link; a link or list removed on purpose stays removed), a file that already has a draft of its own keeps it and the name's old draft goes, and the name lets go only once every copy is kept; when one could not be kept, the move is not marked done and the next page tries again. A file seen later whose hand-over fails gets no id yet: it goes by its name for that page, and its next open tries again. A read that fails stops a hand-over; it is never taken for "nothing there" (second look round 2), also a browser folder that can't be read (`browserHas`). A name the move could not hand over keeps no new ids, so its files go by that name, where the old draft still is, until the next try (second look round 3). Lead's fix round (2026-11-19): while the move is not done on a page (it failed, or the recent list could not be read: `recentInventory` keeps read errors and the move is never marked done after one), a file without an id goes by its name and takes nothing alone (since review round 13: only a file whose name still waits for the move), so the next try hands each name to all its files (SL-1, SL-3; browser checks `migratefull` with two files and `migratelist`); a copy left behind by a move to a file is not a browser script, also while a tab holds it (`browserHas` leaves out `copies.names()`, SL-2; `movedcopy`); a handle looked up before moves to the front of `fileIds` too when it opens again (SL-4). A page whose move failed takes up ids again once another tab has finished it (review on the fix round). All three browser checks failed on b5c06f9. The draft is handed over last, so a hand-over that stops leaves it under the name for the next try (review round 9; browser check `SMOKE_ONLY=migratefull`, which failed on 201224f: one B-roll list copy fails, the name keeps its draft, list and link and the move is not marked done; the next page hands everything over). Save as uses the new file's key only once it is kept in `fileIds` (`adopt` is a promise); where storage refuses, the file goes by its name.
- **Robust as a whole** (Fable's round, 2026-11-19, on the second look's P0 and P1). Where this differs from the lines above, this is how it works now.
  - *The hand-over lives in `script-keys.js`* (`createHandOver`, storage passed in, so the unit tests run all of it). Every read comes before the first write and fails loudly: IndexedDB, the draft in local storage (read as it is stored, never through the quiet `store.get`), a list left in local storage, the browser folder and the names of the copies left behind. A read that fails stops the hand-over with nothing written, nothing deleted and the move unmarked. The P0: the old draft was read through `store.get`, which gives "nothing" for a read that failed, so the draft counted as handed over and was deleted.
  - *Copies first, then the ids, then the name lets go.* `handOver` only copies and gives back `letGo()`. A file seen for the first time: its copies, then its id is kept in `fileIds`, then the name lets go. The move: every name's copies, then the ids of the names that worked, then those names let go, then it is marked done. No id is rolled back any more, and nothing is deleted for a key the next page could not find. A name that can't let go keeps its old keys beside the copies (nothing lost; at the move it is not marked done and the next page finishes it). Letting go takes the draft first and never deletes a draft written under the name since it was copied; of two drafts the one written later stays under the file's key.
  - *One file, one key.* The stored list decides at every open, also for a handle the tab knew before. Save as onto a file that has a key keeps that key (it got a new one before, and a script of that file open or kept aside went on writing under the old one); the draft kept for what the file held before goes. A key the tab still writes under that fell off the list (200 other files) is put back: at that script's next open, at any other open in the tab, and when the tab is looked at again (`keep`, on focus and when the page shows). The P1: both ways a remembered key went stale, and words written under it were lost on reload.
  - *From the review of this round (round 13, both P3, fixed).* A try whose ids could not be kept takes its draft copy back (`letGo.undo`), so no copy piles up in local storage under a key nobody will look up. And only the names the move could not hand over, or that have not let go, wait (`pending` is those names; all names only while the move has not run or its list can't be read): a file of another name gets its key as usual, so one value that never reads does not put every new file back on its name.
  - *Across tabs* (round of 2026-11-20, on the second look's P0 and P1 at 276455f). Other tabs do not wait for a hand-over, and a draft is written to local storage at any moment, outside every lock. Three rules close that family.
    - *The tabs know each other's files in use* (`createInUse`). A page holds a shared Web Lock per file id it has looked up (`script-editor:file-in-use:<id>`), until it goes away; any page can ask which ids are held (`navigator.locks.query`). A page comes to know a key, and so to write under it, only inside the id list's lock and with that lock held.
    - *A file in use never falls off the id list* (the P1: 200 files opened in another tab pushed a file off while its tab was not looked at, and a reload then lost what was kept under its key). The files in use (any tab's, and the scripts this tab has open or kept aside) go to the front at every write of the list: every open, Save as, the move, and when a tab is looked at again. Only the rest is cut to 200. Where it can't be told which ids are held, nothing is cut. The list can hold more than 200 only while living pages have looked up more files than that.
    - *No write in the hand-over trusts a read made before a wait* (the P0: it chose between two drafts, waited for the list and link copies, then wrote, over words another tab kept in that wait). A draft is written under a file's key only while no other tab has that file in use; since no tab can take it up before the id list's lock is given back, that holds until the write. Both drafts are read again right before the write, with no wait in between (this tab's own scripts, and the name). The list and link copies are each looked at and written in one IndexedDB transaction (`idbFill`). A draft that changed, or a file in use elsewhere, stops the hand-over: nothing written over, nothing let go, the move not marked done, and the next page decides again.
  - *Known limits, left as they are.*
    - A file that goes by its name on a page (storage failed at its hand-over, or the move is pending) is the old behaviour by name for that page: when another tab hands that name over meanwhile, what the first tab writes under the name until its next open is not seen by the file later. The same holds for a tab still running the code from before this step while a newer tab does the move: such a tab holds no lock and goes by names, so the newer tab can't see it. After the deploy of this step, reload the editor tabs that were open before it.
    - Words such a by-name tab writes under the name in the instant between the last read and the write are never deleted: letting go stops and the name keeps them. At the move the next page hands them over; for a file seen for the first time they stay under the name, as in the limit above.
    - A browser without Web Locks (none that can open files on the computer) falls back on one tab's view: a key that fell off the list is put back when the tab is looked at again; if another tab gave the file a new id before that, the listed id wins and what was kept under the old one is not carried over.
    - A lock the browser refuses (it has Web Locks, yet a request fails; not seen in practice) never stops an open: that tab still knows its key, but the other tabs can't see that it does. Their hand-over could then copy the name's draft under that key while the tab has the file in use, and the tab's next draft would write over the copy. The lock is asked for again at the file's next open.
    - After a reload or a crash a page holds nothing until it opens its file again; the file was at the front of the list until then, so only some 200 other files opened in that gap would push it off.
- The B-roll part's seam is 3 (`scriptKey` is new in its host).

## Checks

- `tests/script-keys.test.mjs`: one key per file, the same key for the same file through another handle and on the next page, another key for another file of that name, Save as (`adopt`) onto a new file and onto one that has a key (it keeps it), the move of old keys once (files on the list, newest first) and for a file seen later, storage refusing (the file goes by its name and the name lets go of nothing; Save as too), a read that fails (nothing written), a file opened again moving to the front (also when that write fails), and the move tried again on the next page when a hand-over failed.
- `tests/saving.test.mjs`: a left script's failed saves (running or queued, and `saveLeft` meeting a file changed elsewhere) keep the draft under the file's own key while another script.md keeps its own; Save as to a same-named file in another folder moves the keys; a draft that can't be written under its new key stays under the old one.
- `scripts/smoke-several-scripts.mjs`, `SMOKE_ONLY=ownkeys`: two files called script.md; the B-roll list and a "Check" flag kept under the name open in the first; the agent's answer lands in the bread script.md in the background; its own draft has the marked change, a waiting ask and a new "Check" flag; after a reload it opens with the mark, the ask, both flags and Undo on the agent's tag (Undo works); the walk script.md shows only its own list and nothing of the bread one. `SMOKE_ONLY=migrate`: two script.md files on the recent list before the update: both show the list the name had, only the newest offers the old unsaved words. Both failed on 557541f (the code before this step). `SMOKE_ONLY=deletefirst` (review round 1, failed on 2aaf543): a file script.md seen for the first time takes none of a browser script.md's list or words; deleting the browser script.md drops its keys though a file script.md is on the list; the next new file script.md starts clean. `SMOKE_ONLY=reloadheld` (review round 2, failed on 557541f): a reload while the agent still holds an ask in a background script: the ask comes back when it opens, and the answer lands. The same-name checks (`samename`, `deletesame`, `deletekept`) now read each file's own key.
- Fable's round (2026-11-19): 26 unit tests new or rewritten, 21 of them failing on d7bcd07 and 3 more on 24859f9 (review round 13: `undo`, no draft copy left behind, a waiting name waits alone). `tests/script-keys.test.mjs`, the hand-over itself: a draft, a link, a list, a file's own place or the browser folder that can't be read stops it with everything as it was; copies first and nothing deleted until `letGo`; only places never written, a link removed on purpose stays removed, the list before its link, the draft last; of two drafts the newer stays; letting go never deletes a draft written since the copy, and a removal that did not take is an error; a browser script's name; a list left in local storage; the demo. The order of the steps for a file seen for the first time and for the move (copies, ids, let go, done), and each step failing. One key per file: Save as onto a file that has a key, also one kept aside whose key fell off the list; a key that fell off is put back at its next open, by any other open in the tab and by `keep`; a new id from another tab wins at the next open; a known file keeps its key while the list can't be read or written. `tests/saving.test.mjs`: Save as onto a file that has a key clears the draft kept for what it held, also when another script opened meanwhile. Browser checks, all three failing on d7bcd07: `SMOKE_ONLY=migratedraft` (the name's draft can't be read at the move: it was deleted and the move marked done; now the name keeps it, and the next page hands it to the file, which offers "Unsaved changes"), `copiesread` (the names of the copies left behind can't be read: a moved copy was taken for a browser script and kept the draft for good), `samekey` (Export → Markdown file onto a file that has a key keeps that key, one entry; an entry taken off the list is put back when the tab gets focus, and the next page finds the same key).
- Round of 2026-11-20 (the second look's P0 and P1 at 276455f): 15 unit tests new in `tests/script-keys.test.mjs`, 14 of them failing on 276455f (the 15th guards that two tabs looked at in turn do not write the list again). The hand-over: words another tab keeps under the file's key, or under the name, while the copies are made stop it and are never written over; no draft is written under the key of a file another tab has in use, or when that can't be told; a list or link another tab keeps under a file's key meanwhile is not written over. The id list: a file one tab has in use is never pushed off by the files other tabs open, and goes once no tab has it; the scripts in use go to the front when the tab is looked at again and at every open; the move keeps the files in use too; where it can't be told, nothing is let go. `createInUse`: one shared lock per id until the page goes away, every page sees all ids, a page's own hold is not "elsewhere", a lock that can't be had never stops an open and is asked for again, and one tab's stand-in knows its own ids. Browser checks, each with real Web Locks and failing on 276455f (6, 5 and 6 checks): `SMOKE_ONLY=twotabs` (two tabs of one browser: with the list full and the first tab's file at its end, the second tab opens a file; the first tab's file stays, right behind it, and the first tab's next page finds the same key; the lock goes when the tab closes), `handrace` (words kept under the file's key while the move's copies are made: not written over, the name keeps everything, the next page finishes the move and the file offers those words), `handinuse` (the move tried while another tab has the file open: no draft written under its key; once that tab has gone, the next page hands the words over).
- Second look on the release (PR #89, 2026-11-20, P1): Save as onto the script's own file, with another script opened before the file's key came back, deleted the draft kept for the script as the person left it (its asks, marks and "Check" flags; gone after a reload). `saveAs` now remembers the script's own key before any wait and never deletes the draft under it. `tests/saving.test.mjs`, with `adopt` paused until the test lets it answer: that case (failing on 5209394), Save as onto another file left the same way (only the draft kept for what that file held before goes; the script open now keeps its file, name and draft), and Save as of a browser script left the same way (its own draft and its browser copy stay; R7-17). No other delete in `saving.js` goes by a picked file's key.

- Fixed on 2026-11-19 (lead's fix round: a file whose name waits for the move goes by that name and takes nothing alone, `waits` and `pending` in `forFile`; unit test "script keys (SL-1)"). What the finding said: Spec (P2): 64281b4:public/script-keys.js:119 — P2 fault: when the move fails for a name, it now drops the new ids of that name's files, but only for that page. If one of those files opens on the same page, `forFile` (line 64-72) treats it as a file seen for the first time. It then calls `hand(handle.name, [fileKey(id)])` without `moving`, and `legacyPlan` gives `{ broll: [id], draft: id, clear: true }`. If storage works again by then (a short-lived error, or space freed), that one file takes the draft, link and list, and the name lets go of them. On the next page `migrate` runs again for `a/script.md` and `b/script.md`, but nothing is left under the name, so `b/script.md` never gets its copy of the B-roll link and list. That breaks the spec line "each gets a copy of the B-roll link and list". Before this commit, the ids were kept, so `forFile` found the id and did no hand-over, and the next page's move gave both files their copy. Fix: in the `createScriptKeys` closure, keep the names that failed in `migrate`. In `forFile`, for a handle whose name is in that set, return `handle.name` with no id and no hand-over, so the next page's move gives every file of the name its copy. Remove the "(a file opened meanwhile tries again too)" note at line 118, or reword it.
- Fixed on 2026-11-19 (lead's fix round: `browserHas` leaves out the copies listed under `movedCopies`; browser check `SMOKE_ONLY=movedcopy`). What the finding said: Spec (P2): 64281b4:public/app.js:3056 — P2 fault: `browserHas` now looks the name up with `getFileHandle`. That also finds a browser copy left behind by a move to a file, which waits in `movedCopies` until a later listing deletes it. The old check (`browserScripts()` → `copies.list()`) left those copies out. Take a browser `script.md` that was moved to a disk `script.md` before the update, while another tab still had the copy open. Its keys under `script.md` belong to the disk file. At the move, `legacyPlan` now sees `browser: true`, so the disk file gets only the B-roll copy, the name keeps the draft, and `clear` is false. Deleting the left copy later does not hand the draft over. The disk file goes by `file:<id>` and never offers the old words, so the draft stays hidden under `script.md` for good. Fix: before the folder lookup, add `if (copies.names().includes(name)) return false;`, the same list `nameTaken` already uses. That way a left copy waiting for cleanup does not count as a browser script, and a folder that can't be read is still an error.
